evidence.quote: BE IT ENACTED BY THE PEOPLE OF THE STATE OF OKLAHOMA:

summary.short: Amends Oklahoma child pornography statutes (21 O.S. §§ 1021.2, 1024.1, 1040.12a) to criminalize knowing possession, viewing, sharing and other conduct, and to cover computer-generated and altered images appearing to be children. Effective November 1, 2024.
summary.long: Amends three sections of Title 21 of the Oklahoma Statutes on child pornography. Section 1021.2 makes it a felony to procure or cause the participation of a minor in child pornography or obscene material, or knowingly to possess, view, access, share, stream, download, procure, sell, distribute or manufacture child pornography. The penalty is imprisonment of up to 20 years and a fine of up to $25,000, with no deferred sentence and mandatory post-imprisonment supervision for sentences of two years or more. The minor's consent is not a defense. Section 1024.1 extends the definition of child pornography to altered depictions of children and to computer-generated or altered images that appear to be a child and are obscene, defines the related terms, and treats each image as a separate item. Section 1040.12a creates aggravated possession of 100 or more separate visual depictions of child pornography, punishable by imprisonment up to life and a fine of up to $10,000, with registration as a sex offender upon conviction. The act takes effect November 1, 2024.

notes: Bill text (Oklahoma H 3642) with four sections: three amend 21 O.S. 2021 and Section 4 sets the effective date of November 1, 2024. The document is the bill as text, not an enrolled act; it contains no adoption or signature information, so the registry's adopted status is not confirmed by this text. The amended sections are reproduced in full without strike-through or underline markings, so new wording cannot be separated from restated wording; check against the enrolled version before coding obligations or thresholds. Internal drafting issues: Section 1 repeats 'shall be guilty, upon conviction, be guilty of a felony'; Section 1 has 'sold or, distributed' with a misplaced comma; Section 2 writes 'computergenerated' without a hyphen. Section 2 includes computer-generated and altered images within child pornography in 1024.1(A)(3) as worded in the text. Penalty amounts and other enforcement provisions are not recorded in this pass.

obligations.note: The operative provisions are criminal offences and penalties (21 O.S. 1021.2; 1040.12a), which are coded as enforcement rather than obligations. Section 2 is definitional. The sex-offender registration duty in Section 3 follows from conviction and is treated as a penalty consequence. Section 4 sets only the effective date. No regulatory or administrative duties were found.
